source_en: Returning home after a twelve-hour driving shift.
Going home to the western block. Wife and kids are waiting.
Dropping off the car at the fleet garage for repairs.
Cab won't start. Walking home to the western block.
Checking on the security of my apartment building.
Hunting a spare part for the Volga. Engine's dead again.
Going home. Cab's dead in the depot yard. Nothing to drive.
Home to my wife and kids. Nowhere left to drive anyway.
Fulfilling mandatory residency check-in.
First day as a taxi driver. Still learning the streets.
Walking home. Never learned to drive, can't stand cars.
Collecting my pension. Retired from driving last year.
Driving my new car home. Engine purrs like a kitten.
Going home alone. Never married, never wanted kids.
Returning from my desk at the Writers' Union office.
Driving fares all night. Business has never been better.
Going home to the eastern district, where I've always lived.
Going to my mother's. She's the only family I've got.
Move it along, officer. I’ve got a fare waiting and time is money.
What, you need to see my teeth too? Just check the damn paper.
This town is going to hell because everyone’s standing around asking questions.
My car won't start and the streets are full of junk. You happy now?
Don't look at me like that. I’ve dealt with tougher guys than you before breakfast.
You think this booth makes you special? We’re all breathing the same poison.
Go ahead, keep me here. There’s nowhere left to drive anyway.
You’re just a glorified bouncer for a club that’s currently burning down.
I hope you’re proud of your little rubber stamp. It’s all you’ll have left soon.
Finally. Try to work a bit faster next time, yeah?
Yeah, yeah. Watch your back out here. It’s getting ugly.
Whatever. Enjoy your little cage while it lasts.
You’re kidding me. I don't have time for this circus!
Lock me up then. At least I won't have to look at your face.
Fine. It’s probably quieter in there than it is out here.
Hey! What are you...!
I knew you were looking for an excuse to pull that trigger!
About time... someone... shut the world... up.
You have GOT to be out of your mind right now, I swear!
FINE! But I want it on the record that this is completely, absolutely wrong!
At least it’ll be quieter in there than it is out here. Small mercies.
Of all the small-minded, cowardly...!
You better hope… I don’t come back… as a ghost… pal…
Alright… alright… I’ll give you this one… but just… this once…
Where are you coming from?
The fleet garage. Twelve hours behind the wheel and the Volga's clutch is shot again. Can I go?
My building in the western block. Checked the locks, looters everywhere. Cab won't start, so I walked.
Nowhere. The cab's dead in the depot yard. I walked through the ash like everybody else.
My place on the east side. Same route every night, I could drive it blind.
A fare out to Varka and back. Car ran like a dream, roads wide open the whole way.
My brother's flat. I've bunked there since the wife left me. No kids, nothing to go home to.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My nose won't stop running. Twelve hours breathing exhaust will do that. That's it. Next question.
I get dizzy when I stand up too fast. It passes. Don't you write that down.
My ears ring. All day, all night. Could be the sirens, could be me. What does it matter?
Healthy as a horse. Haven't driven in months, so there's no fumes in my lungs.
Two weeks in bed with a fever, doctor's orders. Haven't left the flat once.
Nothing. Clean lungs. I gave up the cab years ago. I push papers at the ispolkom now.
Move it along, would you? I have been standing here twelve minutes.
You need to check the papers or what? I do not have all day.
Someone should sort out the roads into this district. Absolute mess.
My cab does not start anymore. Three years I kept that engine running.
Half the streets are blocked now. You know that, right? Your people closed them.
Do not look at me like that. I am just trying to get home.
Go ahead, take your time. Not like the world is ending or anything.
I have nowhere to drive and nowhere to be. Happy now?
You are still stamping papers. Fine. Stamp the paper. I will wait.
